nodes.summary: The score of a leaf order: the sum of the similarities of adjacent leaves.
nodes.title: Adjacent-similarity score of a leaf order

nodes.summary: Correctness of the optimal leaf ordering recursion (Bar-Joseph, Gifford and Jaakkola 2001): the dynamic program computes, for every end pair `(i, j)`, the best score of a leaf order of `t` starting at `i` and ending at `j`.
nodes.title: Correctness of the optimal leaf ordering recursion

nodes.summary: The dynamic program of Bar-Joseph, Gifford and Jaakkola: `bestEnds S t i j` is computed from the tables of the two children, trying both child orders.
nodes.title: Bar-Joseph–Gifford–Jaakkola dynamic program for leaf ordering

nodes.summary: A rooted binary tree whose leaves are labeled by `α`: the shape of a dendrogram (merge heights are irrelevant for leaf ordering).
nodes.title: Dendrogram as a leaf-labeled binary tree

nodes.summary: One side of the recursion: the left part ranges over orders of a subtree with leaves `Ll` and best-score table `Ml`, the right part over a subtree with leaves `Lr` and table `Mr`; the two are joined at the adjacent pair `(k, l)`.
nodes.title: Joining two subtree orders at an adjacent leaf pair

nodes.summary: The leaves of a dendrogram, left to right.
nodes.title: Leaves of a dendrogram

nodes.summary: A dendrogram with `m` internal nodes has `2 ^ m` leaf orders (one per flip pattern).
nodes.title: A dendrogram with m internal nodes has $2^m$ leaf orders
Number of internal nodes of a dendrogram

nodes.summary: The best score among the leaf orders of `t` that start with `i` and end with `j` (`⊥` if there is none).
nodes.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score with fixed end leaves

nodes.summary: The optimal leaf-ordering score is the best `bestEnds` value over end pairs of leaves.
nodes.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score via the dynamic program

nodes.summary: Every dendrogram has a leaf order, so the optimal score is a real number.
nodes.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score is finite

nodes.summary: The best score among the leaf orders of `t` (never `⊥`: `optScore_ne_bot`).
nodes.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score

nodes.summary: The leaf orders obtained by choosing, at each internal node, which child is drawn first. Each choice pattern contributes one entry, so the list has `2 ^ numInternal t` entries.
nodes.title: Leaf orderings of a dendrogram

nodes.summary: Every leaf order of `t` is a permutation of its leaves.
nodes.title: Leaf orders are permutations of the leaves

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
